0.0.n: This is the name of Japan’s national parliament.

0.1.n: Marks the place where the debate takes place.

0.2.n: Adds a topic-setting emphasis to 国会で, establishing the parliamentary setting.

0.3.n: A family name, followed here by the person’s official title.

0.4.n: Combines with 大臣 to form 総理大臣, the title for Japan’s head of government.

0.5.n: The second part of the official title 総理大臣.

0.6.n: Links Takaichi with the opposition leaders as participants in the debate.

0.7.n: Refers to political parties outside the governing side.

0.8.n: Counts the opposition party leaders taking part.

0.9.n: Refers here to the heads of the six opposition parties.

0.10.n: Connects the participants to 党首討論, identifying who conducts the debate.

0.11.n: Combines with 討論 to name a debate among political party heads.

0.12.n: Together with 党首, names the parliamentary event being reported.

0.13.n: Marks 党首討論 as the event that was held.

0.14.n: A linking form of the passive 行われる, from 行う; it connects this event to the following statement.

1.0.n: In 消費減税, this points to consumption tax, although the usual 税 after 消費 is omitted.

1.1.n: Combines with 消費 to refer specifically to reducing consumption tax.

1.2.n: Shows that consumption tax cuts are one example, not the only topic discussed.

1.3.n: Marks the subject matter of the discussion.

1.4.n: Pairs with 交わす to describe people exchanging views.

1.5.n: Marks 議論 as what was exchanged in this passive sentence.

1.6.n: Polite past passive of 交わす; with 議論, it reports that people exchanged views without naming them again.

0.lit: In the Diet, a party-leader debate by Prime Minister Takaichi and six opposition party leaders was held, and…
0.tip: 行われ is a linking passive form, so the sentence continues rather than ending here.

1.lit: About consumption tax cuts and other issues, discussions were exchanged.
1.tip: 議論が交わされました literally describes discussions being exchanged, naturally meaning that people discussed the issues.
